claim_1.claim: CyTOF analysis of PBMCs from 42 pediatric cases of chikungunya virus infection showed significant expansion of CD14+CD16+ monocytes during the acute phase compared to the convalescent phase.

sources.quote: Clustering by community frequency revealed a distinct contrast in CD14 + CD16 + monocyte frequencies between the acute and convalescent phases (vertical axis, Fig 2 B). This is the most expanded population at the acute timepoint (Fig 2 C), and the difference was highly significant (q‐value, aka false discovery rate‐adjusted P [FDR P ] = 1.7 × 10 −18 ; moderated paired t‐test, mixed‐effects model).

comparison.finding: significant expansion of CD14+CD16+ monocytes during the acute phase compared to the convalescent phase

claim_2.claim: RNA sequencing analysis of whole blood from 42 pediatric cases of chikungunya virus infection showed upregulation of monocyte-associated cytokine genes such as CXCL10 and CCL2 during the acute phase compared to the convalescent phase.

sources.quote: Among CXC‐ and CC‐chemokine subfamilies, we observed transcriptional upregulation of CXCL10 , CXCL11 , CCL2 , and CCL8 ( Appendix Fig S17 ). Of these, monocyte‐secreted CXCL10 and monocyte chemoattractant CCL2 concur with the changes in serum cytokine concentrations described above (Fig 5 A and B).

comparison.finding: upregulation of monocyte-associated cytokine genes such as CXCL10 and CCL2 during the acute phase compared to the convalescent phase

claim_3.claim: Luminex xMAP analysis of serum from 42 pediatric cases of chikungunya virus infection showed significant increases in monocyte chemoattractant CCL2 and other cytokines during the acute phase compared to the convalescent phase.

sources.quote: The strongest contrast was for the monocyte chemoattractant CCL2 (FDR P = 3.6 × 10 −11 ). Significant increases were also observed for IL‐10 (a monocyte‐secreted anti‐inflammatory cytokine), CXCL10 (an IFN‐γ‐inducible monocyte‐secreted cytokine), IFN‐γ, IFN‐α2, TNF‐α, CXCL8 (IL‐8), IL‐1α, IL‐15, G‐CSF, GM‐CSF, CCL4, CCL5, CCL11, CX 3 CL1, IL‐6, IL‐1RA, IL‐12p40, and IL‐2.

comparison.finding: significant increases in monocyte chemoattractant CCL2 and other cytokines during the acute phase compared to the convalescent phase
